newsitem.title: USA: PGA GOLF-FROST WINS BY TWO AS WOODS FALTERS AT COLONIAL.
newsitem.headline: PGA GOLF-FROST WINS BY TWO AS WOODS FALTERS AT COLONIAL.

text.p: David Frost of South Africa won for the first time in nearly three years Sunday, holding on for a two-stroke victory as Tiger Woods faltered at the $1.6 million Colonial golf tournament.

Frost shot a three-under-par 67 for a four-round total of 15-under 265, then sweated it out in the clubhouse as first David Ogrin, then Woods failed to catch him. It was the 10th career victory for Frost, who had been struggling this year and missed the cut at five of the nine tournaments he played.

Frost finished in the top 20 only once this year and wasn't even among the top 150 on the 1997 money list before capturing the $288,000 top prize. His last PGA victory came at the 1994 Greater Hartford Open.

Ogrin, the third-round leader, stumbled to a two-over 72 and fell into a second-place tie with red-hot Brad Faxon, who shot a 70. It was Faxon's third runner-up finish in six weeks and moved him into third place on the money list.
Woods, gunning for his third successive win, trailed by only one stroke heading to the 17th hole.

But he sent his second shot over the green and into a group of trees before chipping into a greenside bunker. He ran his sand shot past the hole, missed the comebacker and took his second double-bogey of the day.

Like Ogrin, Woods had a final-round 72, ending a streak of 10 straight rounds in the 60s that dated back to the first round of the Masters. Woods fell into a fourth-place tie with Paul Goydos, who shared the second-round lead but had a one-over 71 in the final round.
